purpose: Prevents excessive consumption of computational, memory, storage, or third-party service resources that could degrade availability or drive up operating costs.
summary: Unrestricted Resource Consumption occurs when an API doesn't properly limit the size or number of requests, response payloads, or resource-intensive operations a client can trigger, making the API vulnerable to denial of service or excessive operational cost.
expectedStatementElements: What rate limiting is applied per client, user, or API key
What limits exist on request payload size, response size, pagination, and array lengths
What limits or timeouts exist on resource-intensive operations (e.g., long-running queries, file uploads, third-party API calls)
How the API monitors and alerts on abnormal resource consumption patterns
evidenceExamples: Rate limiting configuration per client/user/API key
Request/response size and pagination limit configuration
Timeout and resource-limit configuration for expensive operations
Monitoring or alerting configuration for abnormal consumption spikes
commonGaps: No rate limiting exists, allowing unlimited requests from a single client
No limit on response payload size or pagination, letting a single request return unbounded data
Expensive operations (large file uploads, complex queries) have no size or time limits
No monitoring would catch an unusual spike in resource consumption before it causes an outage or cost spike
interviewQuestions: What stops a single client from sending an unlimited number of requests to this API?
Are there limits on how much data a single request or response can contain?
What happens if someone triggers an expensive operation repeatedly — is there a limit or timeout?
How would you find out about an unusual spike in API resource usage before it causes a problem?
